column1: # Game profile of Paper Mario: The Origami King (Switch, update 1.0.1 = v65536). Plays on the Mac at 30 fps, as on the Switch (the title, a new game, the opening drive into Toad Town and Peach's castle, with sound)
# Intelligent Systems' engine on NintendoWare (G3d, Vfx, Atk), NVN, SDK 8.3.1. Nearly every RomFS file is zstd (named .zst), the music is Opus, and the movies are WebM through the SDK's movie
# library (subsdk0). The shaders are BNSH: 3,763 in shaders/*.bfsha.zst and 5,675 in the particle effects (effect/*.ptcl.zst)

# Game name: only a label for profile listings and the Mac window title; the iOS app name is the game name in the base NSP, and the bundle ID comes from the base game title ID (build_ipa.sh / NSP script)
# only the merged 1.0.1 copy is extracted
# load order as on Horizon: main, subsdk*, sdk (subsdk0 = NintendoSDK_movie)
# The NPDM declares 8 MB of system resource (virtual address memory), and main never calls SetMemoryHeapSize. nninitStartup makes the game's malloc a StandardAllocator over 62 GB of address
# space (the region returns to main+0x5c05ac), which the host's StandardAllocator cap gives 4.06 GB. With the sdk cuts (node area 62 MB, 32 MB alignment for large regions; dm/tools/sdk_patches.py)
# it fits Engage's 5 GB block: 256 MB in front + 4.375 GB alias region + 256 MB stack region + 128 MB heap region (never used). 1.39 GB mapped at boot
# the NPDM declares 8 MB of system resource
# The anti-aliasing pass (shaders/aa.bfsha variation 1) samples the 1920x1080 RGB10A2 scene target it renders into: on the Mac whole 16x16 blocks of it read as magenta (1, 0, 1) in some frames
# (about one block a frame at Peach's castle, none with the snapshot). Once a frame, an 8 MB copy
# ---- Shader split (shader_split.py: BNSH in the zstd .bfsha and .ptcl files) ----
